outcome: Mother-to-child transmission (MTCT) of Hepatitis B virus (HBV)
cohort: 852 HBsAg- and HBeAg-positive mothers who did not receive antiviral treatment during pregnancy and their newborns, recruited from hospitals in China
finding: Both cesarean section and nonbreastfeeding were found to reduce the risk of mother-to-child transmission of Hepatitis B virus in infants of HBsAg- and HBeAg-positive mothers who did not receive antiviral therapy during pregnancy.
mod_finding: Caesarean section showed a tendency to reduce the risk of HBV infection (RR = 0.61) although it did not reach statistical significance.
